sanity_expectations: N_next is non-negative and finite over the whole sampled region
As a function of N at fixed T=T_opt, moderate P: unimodal (hump-shaped) - rises near-linearly at low N then falls due to overcompensating crowding (exp(-alpha*N)) and predation
N_next declines as |T - T_opt| increases (Gaussian thermal response)
At fixed N and T, N_next increases with P (wetter conditions relax both desiccation loss and the moisture-modulated mortality term)
New term suppresses N_next most strongly at high N and low P; dropping gamma_wet to 0 raises N_next in that regime
excitation_report: sigma=1.0 (absolute std on N_next). Single dominant multiplicative recruitment term: RMS 20.8x sigma. New term (E - parent = moisture-enhanced density-dependent mortality factor 1/(1+(N/N_refuge)^q_pred*exp(-gamma_wet*P/(P+P_wet_half)))): peak effect 17.5x sigma, strongest at N~50.6, P~13.2 (dry / high-density regime), T~19.9 (near T_opt). auto_balance converged=true, all terms visible; no rebalancing required.
role_corrections: N_next: output->output (confirmed: LHS, explicitly solvable target)
N: input->independent variable (confirmed: current-generation density, primary sampling axis)
R0: P->P (confirmed: fixed max reproductive rate)
gamma_wet: P->P (confirmed: moisture-mortality amplitude, hint range 0-5)
P_wet_half: P->P (confirmed: wet half-saturation, hint range 10-150)
rationale: Explicit stock-recruitment (Ricker-type) map from current to next-generation abundance. N_next is the LHS target; N, T, P are the natural measured axes across many densities/climates and receive sampling ranges; all other symbols are fixed physical constants. Parameter values chosen for overcompensating single-hump dynamics (R0=10, alpha=0.02 so alpha*N ranges 0-3), moderate Allee (N_allee=5), predation onset near N_refuge=40 with Hill q_pred=2, thermal optimum T_opt=20 with beta_temp=0.02 giving meaningful falloff across 10-30 C, and moisture terms within suggested hints (gamma_wet=3 in [0,5], P_wet_half=50 in [10,150]). Verified finite/real at a representative point; excitation confirms both the dominant term and the newly added moisture-enhanced density-dependent mortality term are well above noise.

scenario_text: A univoltine insect population is censused once per generation, where crowding within a generation strongly depresses the number of survivors reproducing in the next. At low density nearly all reproduce, but overcompensating crowding sharply reduces recruitment at high density. Ecologists collect paired successive-generation abundance measurements across many densities. The target is the mapping from one generation's abundance to the next generation's expected abundance.
